title: Mickey Rooney on drums, Jackie Cooper and MGM's big office
summary: Willard and Lee discuss Rooney learning drums, Jackie Cooper being the actor who could play, and who agreed to Lee's terms.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So Mickey Rooney never had played any drums until then.
No. No. He didn't play drums until then. But after that, you know, he started fooling with them quite a bit.

The guy that could play of those movie actors was Jackie Cooper. He was the one that could play, because he used to always come in to clubs and we'd let him sit in. But the rest of them, they had to have somebody play for them.
Who was it you drove your bargain with? Who was it that agreed to your terms?

Well, George Estolle really agreed to them, you know, but we were in Mr. Mayer's office; I never will forget, because we went right in there, they took me right in the Big Man's office. And someone else was the Big Man there, Talmadge or something -- Norman Talmadge -- someone like that, but MGM was really the biggest studio in Hollywood then.
